main_text.head: PRÆLECTIO QUINTA. IN QUA, DE Legum Humanarum Obligatione in ge-nere, Quæstio pertractatur.
ROM. XIII. 5.

head.i: Quare Subjici necesse est, non solum propter Iram, sed etiam propter Conscientiam.

main_text.p: I.DE Obligatione Conscientiæ Passivâ tractationem exorsus superiori Termino, hactenus progressus sum, ut retectis ante rejectisque illis latibulis in quibus inesse aliquid præsidii ad Conscientiæ suæ sive fructum quoad jam facta, sive securitatem quoad faciendā[?], frustra sibi blandiuntur vulgus hominum (boni sc. finis Intentione, & alieni Exempli judiciive authoritate,) propriam illam & adæquatam Conscientiæ regulam, cui se absolutè & simpliciter conformare teneatur, Investigarem. Ubi oftendi Primò 1. Deum solum in Conscientias hominum merum & 2. directum imperium habere: Secundò, Conscientiæ Re-gulam proximam & immediatam esse Lumen mentis pro tempore præsens, sive (quod idem est,){'} ulti-mum judicium intellectus practici. Tertiò, Verbum Dei Scriptum esse quidem supremam & primariam, [illegible, ~20 letters] Aristot. 7. Ethic. 5. 3.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right: "1.", "2." and "3." are section numbers; the Greek note (marked ') is illegible here and was not read. "Aristot. 7. Ethic. 5." is a reference. The "I." at the start of the paragraph stands in the left margin beside the initial D, so it is given as a note; if it is a section number of the text, it may belong in the paragraph. The reference mark ' in the text is doubtful in position. The final letter of "faciendā" is uncertain. The catchword "non" and the signature "I 3" are at the foot. The strip on the far left is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. No running head is printed, since the page opens a division.
